messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: release v2026.03.21.1 -> us-west (rolling canary 5%)

jamie: hey all, saw a p95 jump in the synth wave for the canary group ~10:42 PT, up from ~120ms to ~360ms :thinking_face:

maria: link to dashboards?

jamie: https://dash.internal/redwood/smoke?panel=canary-p95 (zoomed 10m) — spiky fanout across 3 hosts, not all replicas

alex: can you paste the probe request? want to replay locally

jamie: probe is simple health+generate, here's the curl we use:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://smoke.internal/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":8}'
```

kevin: interesting — suspect kv cache warmup on new instances. latency correlates with embed cache misses in the logs I pulled.

maria: recommend pausing the rollout for now and pin canary traffic to previous variant, confirm if we should rollback whole release or hold and investigate

alex: can we reproduce by hitting the canary host directly? if it's KV warmup we should see steady drop with retries.

jamie: tried direct to host ip-10-0-8-23, same tail latencies on cold runs. retries help but p95 still higher than baseline.

oncall-bot: @maria @jamie Autocreated incident INC-2026-03-21-07: "Canary synth p95 spike" — paging oncall rotation.

maria: i'm +1 to hold and pin. we shouldn't rollout until we confirm it's not a regression in runtime patch (kernel/kpack) that landed in this build.

kevin: quick mitigation: enable aggressive prefill for canary instances (kv.prefill=true) and re-run synthetic sweep. if that drops p95 to baseline we can live with a config hotfix.

jamie: can you flip config or we want a rollback? we have 2 options:
- revert to v2026.03.21.0 across canary (quick rollback)
- keep code, flip prefill config and validate (hotfix patch)

alex: timebox 30m for config test. if not green, we rollback.

maria: agreed. @deploy-bot, pause rollout and pin canary to previous version. document action in release notes.

deploy-bot: Action: Pausing rollout. Canary fraction frozen at 5%. Pinned canary route -> v2026.03.21.0. Autoscaler disabled for canary group. (cmd id: cbf-7731)

kevin: flipped kv.prefill=true on canary instances (config push id cfg-9921). kicking off synthetic sweep now.

jamie: running sweep (10 probes per host)

jamie: initial sweep: p95 back to ~140ms after prefill, a few hosts still 200-260ms but trending down 

alex: that suggests warmup/cold-cache problem rather than model regression

maria: ok, since prefill fixes most of it, do a staged config rollout + note in release notes that a prefill flag was required for compat with new runtime. capture the command used and time.

jamie: created a short release-note line: "Hotfix: enable kv.prefill on new runtime to stabilize cold-start latency in small fleets" — will append to release_notes.md in the release PR.

maria: file a follow-up to investigate why new instances start cold (warmup missing?) and whether we should backfill prefill into autoscaler config. assign to runtime team.

oncall-bot: Metric summary: canary p95 before: 120ms, spike peak: 360ms, after prefill sweep: 140ms (10min aggregate).

maria: thanks. we'll keep the canary pinned for one more hour and then resume rollout if no regressions. can anyone volunteer to watch the next sweep?

alex: i'll monitor dashboards for next 30m.

kevin: i'll run a follow-up load-pass and collect KV hit-rate snapshots for the run.

jamie: noted. updating incident with mitigation steps and closing as "mitigated, under observation" — INC-2026-03-21-07. :white_check_mark:

maria: good work all. short postmortem to runtime team: include warmstart sequence, prefill thresholds, and whether to make prefill default for this variant.

deploy-bot: Rollout remains paused. To resume: `deploy-bot resume cbf-7731` (requires two approvers).
